core_obligations: The author geometric improvement for multi-ray stars is only the starting point. Asymmetric anisotropic competitors require a no-island/no-lake analysis, quantitative intersections of Jordan boundaries and three-point slicing to isolate triple junctions; roundedness and Dini or Holder control then yield the original arc regularity.

dedup.scope: Same-source public2201 is uniform perimeter improvement of radial cluster stars with more than three rays. Selected main is full Steiner regularity of minimizing clusters under the original growth/epsilon-epsilon-beta/Dini assumptions, including local finiteness of triple junctions and C1 (or specified C1gamma) arcs. The radial-star tool is retained support, not re-counted. Holder and borderline-Dini regimes belong to one main theorem.

compared.distinction: Local radial competitor improvement versus global local-boundary/Jordan/triple-junction and arc regularity conclusion.
